caption:
Why you pay for the bank's insurance: PMI, explained simply.

What it is: private mortgage insurance. Put less than 20% down on a conventional loan and you pay it, but it protects the lender, not you. With a small down payment the lender has more on the line if you stop paying; PMI covers that risk so the lender can say yes.

Where it came from: modern PMI dates to 1957, when a Milwaukee attorney started a company to insure these loans. The Homeowners Protection Act of 1998 gave borrowers the right to cancel it.

Who chooses it: house hackers buying a place to live with a small down payment, and investors who'd rather keep cash for repairs or the next deal.

Count it in your numbers. It's part of your monthly payment, and leaving it out makes a deal look better than it is.

The good news: you can request cancellation at 20% equity (based on the original value), and it ends automatically at 22%. FHA mortgage insurance has different rules.
